name: Yellowstone National Park (UNESCO)
description: Inscribed 1978. Vast natural forest covering nearly 9,000 km2 containing half of all the world known geothermal features and unparalleled subalpine wildlife.

name: Grand Canyon National Park (UNESCO)
description: Inscribed 1979. Carved by the Colorado River, among the most spectacular gorges in the world with horizontal strata tracing 2 billion years of geological history.

name: Mesa Verde National Park (UNESCO)
description: Inscribed 1978. A great concentration of ancestral Pueblo Indian dwellings built from the 6th to the 12th century, including famous cliff dwellings.

name: Statue of Liberty (UNESCO)
description: Inscribed 1984. A masterpiece of the human spirit gifted by France to the United States, designed by Bartholdi and Eiffel, standing as a universal symbol of freedom.

name: Independence Hall (UNESCO)
description: Inscribed 1979. The Declaration of Independence (1776) and the Constitution of the United States (1787) were debated and signed in this building.

name: Yosemite National Park (UNESCO)
description: Inscribed 1984. Outstanding scenic beauty sculpted by glaciation, with granite domes, waterfalls, clear streams, giant sequoia groves, and biological diversity.

name: Cahokia Mounds State Historic Site (UNESCO)
description: Inscribed 1982. The largest pre-Columbian settlement north of Mexico, occupied during the Mississippian period (800–1400 CE) featuring Monks Mound.

name: Monticello and the University of Virginia (UNESCO)
description: Inscribed 1987. Thomas Jefferson plantation home Monticello and his ideal academical village at the University of Virginia, exemplary neoclassical architecture.

name: Taos Pueblo (UNESCO)
description: Inscribed 1992. Continuous adobe multi-storied pueblo settlement built by the Pueblo Indians in the valley of a small tributary of the Rio Grande.

name: San Antonio Missions (UNESCO)
description: Inscribed 2015. Group of five 18th-century Spanish colonial frontier mission complexes along the San Antonio River, including Mission Concepción and Mission San José.

name: The 20th-Century Architecture of Frank Lloyd Wright (UNESCO)
description: Inscribed 2019. Eight buildings designed by Frank Lloyd Wright illustrating organic architecture, including Fallingwater, the Guggenheim Museum, and Unity Temple.

name: Hopewell Ceremonial Earthworks (UNESCO)
description: Inscribed 2023. A series of eight monumental earthen enclosure complexes built between 2,000 and 1,600 years ago along the central tributaries of the Ohio River.

name: Machu Picchu (UNESCO)
description: Inscribed 1983. 15th-century Inca citadel situated on an Andes mountain ridge 2,430 meters above sea level above the Sacred Valley.

name: Taj Mahal (UNESCO)
description: Inscribed 1983. An immense mausoleum of white marble, built in Agra between 1631 and 1648 by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his favourite wife.

name: Historic Centre of Rome and Colosseum (UNESCO)
description: Inscribed 1980. Founded according to legend in 753 BCE, contains major monuments of antiquity such as the Forum, the Mausoleums of Augustus and Hadrian, and the Colosseum.

name: Angkor (UNESCO)
description: Inscribed 1992. One of the most important archaeological sites in South-East Asia, containing the magnificent remains of the different capitals of the Khmer Empire.

name: Petra (UNESCO)
description: Inscribed 1985. Inhabited since prehistoric times, the Nabataean rock-cut caravan-city carved into red sandstone cliffs features Al-Khazneh (The Treasury).

name: Great Wall of China (UNESCO)
description: Inscribed 1987. Continuously built from the 3rd century BCE to the 17th century CE as defensive fortifications stretching over 20,000 kilometres.

name: Serengeti National Park (UNESCO)
description: Inscribed 1981. Sprawling plains hosting the annual migration of two million wildebeest, plus zebras, gazelles, and major predator populations.

name: Galápagos Islands (UNESCO)
description: Inscribed 1978. A living museum of evolution and showcase of biodiversity in the Pacific Ocean that inspired Charles Darwin theory of evolution by natural selection.
